item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
I don't think there can be a true, valid response for that. When i was writing, I viewed it as stone-cold fact. This is what is happening in black and white, but through a narrator who isn't seeing or reporting everything, and is…unbalanced, to say the least. However, it's also very possible that it's all a hallucination, or even a false document created by The Foundation to keep people from looking too closely in to the actual process.

I think that's the central issue with the "is this real?" question: The Foundation is a endless onion of mind screws and misdirection. Even well-established staff have no idea what is really going on in many cases, and The Foundation keeps up so many mis-direction programs that it's impossible to say for sure what is and is not real, even if you think you know for sure.

Like most staff, it will boil down to you: Is the procedure so nasty and insane that this story is the more sanitized and censored alternative, put in place as a warning and deterrent? Or is this a true record of a insane, dieing man, who may or may not be in the grips of progressive hallucination? Or is it a total dummy, made to throw the reader totally off the "scent". It's really up to you…

Just adding my own comment to the discussion…

A question: Where does he rape her? At what point does the narrator actually engage in anything that may be considered intercourse? I'm honestly asking, as i attempted to make anything overtly sexual so odd or poorly described that it's almost unrecognizable.

Also, some things to consider:

  1. What is it that is growing in that girl's belly that exposing her to people like this is the good option?
  2. At the end, who is lying, the narrator or The Foundation?
  3. Is the change in the narrator a hallucination, the effect of whatever it is in the girl's belly, or a effect from the "funny taste" in the food?

Thanks for all the comments, as well. I admit, knowing that i was able to make at least one person really freak out badly makes this worthwhile.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
Hi all who replied.

After a long period to calm down, I'd like to apologize for reacting the way I did. Horror is supposed to bring up a strong reaction and, obviously, mission freaking accomplished; even seriously twisted and disturbing things like this have literary merit, so and as long as there are clear NSFW1/NSFSS2/NSFAPCSWYR3 warnings wherever the permanent link to this gets posted, there's nothing wrong with it being here. It's not like this is required reading, after all.

Anyway, I'm sorry for flipping out and I'll try not to do it again.

1 - Not Safe For School
2 - Not Safe For Sensitive Stomachs
3 - Not Safe For Anywhere People Can See What You Read

Someone has to bring up this point, and it might as well be me.

I really think it would have been better to let 110-Montauk remain merely implied. Actually featuring explicit child-rape stories, whatever the in-canon or out-of-canon justification, just seems to be going way too far, even for a horror site.

This is the internet. There are real sicko pedophile monsters out here. It's one thing to know they can find this place, read an implication that child rape takes place, and then jerk off to fantasies of their own that fill in the blanks. Knowing that there's actual descriptions of it to give them their sick jollies? No, just … please, no. Nonononono. The Foundation is stained in canon by terrible neccessity. That doesn't mean it's okay to stain the real-world site this way.
